cli.usage:
usage: mcp_n4.server [-h] [--allow-writes] [--write-scope ORD_PREFIX]
                     [--state-dir STATE_DIR] [--token-ttl SECONDS]
                     [--max-writes N] [--auth-cooldown SECONDS]
                     [--load-wait SECONDS] [--http-timeout SECONDS]
                     [--station NAME=URL] [--station-home NAME=PATH]
                     [--credential-env PREFIX] [--insecure-tls NAME]
                     [--allow-tier-b NAME] [--allow-tier-c NAME]
                     [--progress-file PATH] [--allow-http-for-tests]
cli.help:
usage: mcp_n4.server [-h] [--allow-writes] [--write-scope ORD_PREFIX]
                     [--state-dir STATE_DIR] [--token-ttl SECONDS]
                     [--max-writes N] [--auth-cooldown SECONDS]
                     [--load-wait SECONDS] [--http-timeout SECONDS]
                     [--station NAME=URL] [--station-home NAME=PATH]
                     [--credential-env PREFIX] [--insecure-tls NAME]
                     [--allow-tier-b NAME] [--allow-tier-c NAME]
                     [--progress-file PATH] [--allow-http-for-tests]

Stdio MCP server for Niagara N4 stations (newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0). Run
from `mcp-n4-kit/` with `python3 -m mcp_n4.server`. Importing this module has
no side effects; `main()` is only called under `__main__`. MCP protocol
versions: this server speaks 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05
(`SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS`). A client asking for a newer revision is
answered with 2025-06-18. Only add a newer revision to that tuple once its
semantics (new message shapes, capabilities, required fields) are implemented
and tested here.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --allow-writes        register the write tools (dry run + confirmation token
                        each)
  --write-scope ORD_PREFIX
                        ORD prefix writes may touch (repeatable); none = no
                        writes
  --state-dir STATE_DIR
                        journal/audit directory (default
                        ~/.local/state/mcp-n4)
  --token-ttl SECONDS   confirmation token lifetime (default 300)
  --max-writes N        executed writes allowed per server process (default
                        200); a reconnect does not reset it
  --auth-cooldown SECONDS
                        after an authentication failure, refuse station calls
                        this long (default and minimum 30: the lock-out
                        window)
  --load-wait SECONDS   total wait for one component load (default 3; 1-60):
                        raise it for a slow or remote station
  --http-timeout SECONDS
                        HTTP timeout of one station request (default 20;
                        5-300)
  --station NAME=URL    station n4_connect may use (repeatable); NAME should
                        equal the station's stationName; URL must be https://
  --station-home NAME=PATH
                        directory holding the config.bog of configured station
                        NAME; lets n4_save_station prove persistence
                        (repeatable)
  --credential-env PREFIX
                        env var prefix holding <PREFIX>_USER/<PREFIX>_PASSWORD
                        (default MCP_N4)
  --insecure-tls NAME   skip TLS certificate verification for this configured
                        station (self-signed); repeatable
  --allow-tier-b NAME   let writes run on configured station NAME although its
                        version is tier B (4.15/4.3); only after a PoC matched
                        that build (METHODOLOGY section 5); repeatable
  --allow-tier-c NAME   let writes run on configured station NAME although its
                        version is tier C (other or unknown); only after
                        reg.loadContract, loadRoot and a harmless scratch
                        write succeeded; repeatable
  --progress-file PATH  append JSON progress lines of long reads
                        (n4_inventory) to PATH
  --allow-http-for-tests
                        permit http:// base URLs (fake station in tests only)

read_tools.name: n4_connect
read_tools.description: Open a session to one of the stations the operator configured at server start (replaces any previous session). The URL, credentials and TLS policy are fixed by the operator and cannot be chosen here. The station's real stationName must equal expected_station (default: the configured station NAME), or the session is closed. Reports the detected version (oBIX productVersion) and its tier: A (4.13/4.14) writes; B (4.15/4.3) and C (other or unknown) refuse writes unless the operator opted the station in.

expected_station.description: Required stationName; default: the station NAME

read_tools.name: n4_describe_session
read_tools.description: Report whether a station session is active, which station, its version tier, and the server mode. Works without a session.

read_tools.name: n4_navigate
read_tools.description: List the children of a component (name, type, handle, has_children). depth > 1 nests grandchildren under a 'children' key. elapsed_ms is the load time. For a station inventory use n4_bql_query or n4_inventory instead: one navigate is one round trip per component. types (optional) keeps only children whose type is one of the given specs (e.g. bacnet:BacnetDevice) plus the path to them; each kept entry then carries matched true/false. has_children ignores the types filter: it is true when the entry has any component child, matching or not.

types.description: Optional type specs to keep, e.g. ['bacnet:BacnetDevice']; default: no filter

read_tools.name: n4_read_slots
read_tools.description: Read all slots of one component as {name, type, value, status}. Status complexes add status_ok/status_null; omitted values take the type default. value_display carries the station's display string; a complex the reader cannot decode (e.g. a Modbus FlexAddress) returns that display string as value. elapsed_ms is the load time.

read_tools.name: n4_list_links
read_tools.description: List baja:Link / baja:ConversionLink links of components up to depth levels below ord. source_path is null when the source handle is outside the loaded subtree.

depth.description: Component levels below ord to scan (1-4)

read_tools.name: n4_find_dangling_outputs
read_tools.description: List components (up to depth levels below ord) with an 'out' slot that no link in the subtree uses as a source. Links from outside the subtree are not seen. A source ORD that is neither a handle nor an absolute slot path cannot be resolved: outputs it may feed are listed as unknown, not dangling.

depth.description: Component levels below ord to scan (1-4)

read_tools.name: n4_bql_query
read_tools.description: Bulk read: one projected BQL select over a subtree, returned as rows (one HTTP GET, usually under a second, where a navigate crawl costs one round trip per component). Use it FIRST for any inventory. Only 'select <cols> from <type> [where ...]' is accepted; '|' is refused. Columns are the station's display headers (e.g. 'Slot Path', 'Name'; a localized station translates them, a repeated header becomes 'Type#2'); the queried name column is decoded ($20 -> space), 'Slot Path' stays ORD-ready. Proxy-extension fields project as proxyExt.<slot>, e.g. proxyExt.dataAddress. Rows are capped (truncated=true when cut).

base.description: Subtree ORD or slot path, e.g. station:|slot:/Drivers (default: the station root)

query.description: select <columns> from <type> [where ...], e.g. select slotPath, name, out from control:ControlPoint

output_file.description: Optional plain file name (.csv or .json): the rows go to <state-dir>/bql/<name> (0600, never overwritten) instead of the reply

read_tools.name: n4_inventory
read_tools.description: Station inventory through three BQL queries: networks, devices and points below base (default /Drivers), counted per network and per device. A network's built-in local device slot (localDevice, e.g. SnmpNetwork's own agent) is flagged local=true and counted apart from field devices. progress lists each step's row count; the operator's --progress-file gets the same lines.

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per query in seconds

read_tools.name: n4_read_file
read_tools.description: Read one station file (e.g. a Px view file:^px/General.px) through the station's file servlet: GET /file/<path>. file_ord is a file:^ ORD or a path relative to the station home. Refused before any request: '..', '|', ':', absolute paths, directories, names ending in '.' or ' ' and .bog/.bog.gz (the station never serves them). Text types (px, xml, nav, chart, json, csv, html, txt, ...) return text; other files return size, sha256 and content type only (output_file saves the complete bytes under <state-dir>/files/). status is ok, forbidden (403: no read permission) or not_found (404); a 401 pauses station calls and is never retried. Reads are capped at max_bytes (truncated=true, sha256 null when cut).

output_file.description: Optional plain file name with an extension: the complete bytes go to <state-dir>/files/<name> (0600, never overwritten)

read_tools.name: n4_list_px_views
read_tools.description: List the Px views (baja:PxView) below root with one BQL query: display_name, px_file (the file:^ ORD to pass to n4_read_file / n4_px_summary) and media. A PxView is a property value, not a component, so the station usually answers its slot path as NULL: slot_path and owner_path are null then (see owner_note).

read_tools.name: n4_px_summary
read_tools.description: Fetch one .px file (like n4_read_file) and summarize it without returning the XML: media, imported modules, canvases and viewSize, layers, widget and binding type counts, bound ORDs grouped by component (a trailing value slot such as /out stripped), images, included Px files, charts, other ORDs and label texts. Every list is capped at max_items. A file larger than max_bytes is refused, not summarized in part.

read_tools.name: n4_list_batches
read_tools.description: List the write batches in this server's journal, newest first: batch_id, tool, station_name, ts, state (completed / in-doubt), verdict, rollback_of and rolled_back_by. Use it to find the batch_id for n4_rollback. A journal line that cannot be read is listed in unreadable and the reply says the list is incomplete. Reads the journal only; works without a session.

read_tools.name: n4_session_retro_draft
read_tools.description: Draft the session retro: reads this server's audit and journal and returns markdown plus evidence-backed CANDIDATE kit deltas (refusals, bad read-back verdicts, in-doubt batches, BOX errors, dangling outputs). Proposes only; never applies or stages anything. The window starts at the server start; pass since (ISO-8601, e.g. 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z for the whole history) to change it.

since.description: ISO-8601 timestamp; only newer entries are considered (default: when this server started)

write_tools.name: n4_create_component
write_tools.description: Add a component under parent_ord (optionally with a wire sheet position). Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

name.description: Requested slot name (the station may rename on collision)

wire_sheet.description: Optional {x, y, w} wire sheet annotation (integers; w defaults to 8)

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_set_slot
write_tools.description: Set one slot to a value. Status slots are always written whole (value and status). Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

value.description: New value (number, boolean or string by value_type)

value_type.description: One of baja:Double, baja:Boolean, baja:String, baja:StatusNumeric, baja:StatusBoolean

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_invoke_action
write_tools.description: Invoke a control action. Only set, active, inactive, auto are allowed in this version. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

arg_type.description: baja:Double or baja:Boolean, only for set

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_create_link
write_tools.description: Create a link from a source slot to a target slot. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_remove_component
write_tools.description: Remove the child `name` of parent_ord with its whole subtree. The plan snapshots the subtree to depth 3 (type, plain slots, wsAnnotation, links inside it) as the inverse; n4_rollback can re-create only that snapshot, not a full restore. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

link_scan_ord.description: Optional wider ORD (inside the write scope) to scan for links from the subtree into components outside it

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_rollback
write_tools.description: Undo a journaled batch by running its recorded inverse through the same dry run / token pipeline, as a new batch linked to the original. Refuses unknown, already rolled back, in-doubt and other-station batches. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

batch_id.description: batch_id returned by an earlier write

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)

write_tools.name: n4_save_station
write_tools.description: Save the station (persist the running config to disk). The BOX reply proves nothing; persisted is true/false/unknown from config.bog when the server has --station-home for this station. Dry run by default; to execute, repeat the call with dry_run=false and the confirmation_token from the dry run.

dry_run.description: true (default) returns the plan and a confirmation_token without touching the station; false executes and needs that token

confirmation_token.description: Token returned by the matching dry run (single use)
